q: The Nasdaq rose 6.51% while the Dow rose 3.01% after Huang's return. What best explains the gap?
options: The Dow holds more energy firms, which fell as crude lost 4.29%
The Nasdaq holds more AI-linked tech, which reacted most to Huang's return
The Dow holds more tech firms, which reacted most to Huang's return
The Nasdaq holds more food makers, which gained as oil got cheaper
explain: The Nasdaq is packed with AI-linked tech, so the Nvidia news hit it hardest. The Dow has much less of that exposure, so it rose by less.

q: Last week AI worries pulled Treasury yields lower. Why did the 10-year edge up 1 bp to 4.92% today?
options: Oil's drop to 80.38 stirred up fresh inflation worries for bond buyers
Fear-driven buying of safe Treasuries faded as stocks bounced back
Japan sold Treasuries to raise dollars for buying yen in the market
Williams announced a rate hike for the Dec 8 and 9 meeting
explain: Worried investors had bought safe Treasuries last week, which pushed yields down. When stocks recovered that safe-haven demand cooled, so yields stopped falling.

q: The VIX fell 25.83% to 26.62, so the debrief calls the market fully calm again.
options: True
False
explain: The VIX fell a lot, but 26.62 is still a fairly nervous level. Fear eased without disappearing.

q: The 10-year yield is 4.92% and the 2-year is 4.63%, a +29 bp gap. If inflation stays supply-driven and hawkish Fed talk lifts the 2-year more than the 10-year, what happens to that gap?
options: Up
Down
explain: Supply-driven inflation passes less into long-term yields, so the 2-year would catch up to the 10-year. That narrows the gap, which is called flattening, even though both yields might rise.

q: Kroger and Tyson were among the S&P 500's biggest losers as money chased growth. If the AI rally stalls on Nvidia scrutiny, what would these safer stocks probably do?
options: Up
Down
explain: They had been a hiding place amid cracks in the AI trade, so they sold off when the mood flipped. If the rally stalls, investors would likely drift back into them.

q: Goldman's technical read says the dollar index at 104.32 is overbought. If traders suddenly doubt the Fed will keep leaning hawkish, what would the dollar index probably do?
options: Up
Down
explain: Headlines credit the rally to hawkish Fed bets, not the election. If those bets cool, the extra yield from holding dollars shrinks, and an overbought dollar can fall quickly.

q: Put today's AI chain in order, from cause to effect.
items: Nvidia's board approves Huang's return after Trump's pressure
AI-linked stocks like Nvidia and Oracle jump
explain: The CEO news restored confidence, which lifted AI stocks, which lifted the indexes. Lower fear then showed up in the VIX.

q: Put the Fed-to-dollar chain in order, from cause to effect.
items: Williams says higher rates are likely over time
Markets price some hikes, with the 2-year at 4.63%
Dollars look more attractive to hold
explain: The hawkish message raised hike expectations, which made dollar assets pay more than other currencies. That pulled money into the dollar and lifted the index.

q: Headlines credit the dollar index's 0.49% rise to the Democratic midterm rout.
options: True
False
explain: Headlines credit hawkish Fed bets, not the election. The midterms started the dollar story, but today's move came from rate expectations.

q: The St. Louis Fed found hyperscalers' debt relative to assets fell to roughly 25% by early 2026, below other US firms near 34%.
options: True
False
explain: The ratio fell from nearly 30% in 2023 to roughly 25%, while other firms stayed near 34%. So the AI buildout is mostly funded by profits and not by extra borrowing.

q: How should a trader read Lagarde's 'Acting in time' speech, her last at the Frankfurt banking congress?
options: She said the ECB will cut rates to cushion Europe from energy costs
She told banks the ECB will hike its 2.5% rate at the next meeting
She urged acting early on problems, with no hint of an imminent move
She argued Europe should wait for problems to be obvious before acting
explain: Her theme was acting before a problem is obvious, but nothing in the headlines says the ECB is about to move. It's a theme and not a rate signal.

q: The 2-year yield is 4.63% while the Fed's rate is 3.875%. What does that gap tell you?
options: The Fed has already lifted its rate up to 4.63%
Markets already expect the Fed to raise rates over time
Bond buyers think Williams' 2027 inflation view is wrong
Investors expect the Fed to cut rates before 2027
explain: The 2-year tracks expected Fed policy closely. Sitting well above the current rate means traders already price in some hikes.

q: A San Francisco Fed paper says Fed surprises pass less into long yields when inflation is supply-driven. Why does that matter now?
options: Stock gains of 4.73% mean longer yields will now fall sharply this week
Oil-driven inflation means hawkish talk may lift the 2-year more than the 10-year
The Fed can fix oil shortages by raising short-term rates more quickly
Falling oil at 80.38 means inflation is now purely demand-driven again
explain: Inflation is partly driven by oil supply, so hawkish Fed news should show up mostly in short yields. That could flatten the +29 bp curve.

q: The dollar index rose 0.49% but USD/JPY slipped 0.49% to 158.93. What does the debrief say about the yen's move?
options: Japan stepped in again with a record intervention today
The BOJ raised its 1.25% rate to match the Fed's move
Weak Japanese inflation data cut the dollar's appeal
The reason isn't clear, since the dollar was broadly stronger
explain: The yen gained a little even though the dollar was stronger against most currencies, and the headlines don't explain why. So the honest answer is that the cause is unclear.

q: Kroger and Tyson Foods were among the S&P 500's biggest losers as Nvidia surged. What does that suggest?
options: Rising 10-year yields made staples too costly for investors to hold
Money left hiding places and went back into growth stocks
Cheaper oil at 80.38 squeezed food companies' profit margins
Consumers cut spending as the Fed hinted at higher interest rates
explain: Consumer stocks had been a safe bet amid cracks in the AI trade. When AI confidence returned, investors sold them to buy growth, so the move shows how fast the mood flipped.

q: WTI fell 4.29% to 80.38, its lowest settle since August. What drove the drop, according to the debrief?
options: China becoming the top oil buyer cut worldwide demand for crude
Crude kept flowing out of the Persian Gulf despite tanker attacks
Tanker attacks stopped and Gulf shipping returned to normal
Trump's remark about a giant hoax calmed worried oil traders
explain: Attacks on shipping continue, but oil kept leaving the Gulf anyway, so supply fear faded and prices fell. The other options blame events that don't explain today's move.
